Als: um fato no passado, passo a passo: Als: a single event in the past, step by step
PASSO 1: «ALS» (quando) liga a principal: STEP 1: «ALS» (when) links the main clause to a SINGLE EVENT in the past or to a closed period of the past: «Als ich ankam, regnete es» (when I arrived, it was raining), «Als ich Kind war, wohnte ich in einem Dorf» (when I was a child, I lived in a village). STEP 2: «als» opens a SUBORDINATE clause: the conjugated verb goes to the END, and the main clause follows with its verb in 2nd position. STEP 3: tenses: Präteritum, Perfekt or Plusquamperfekt: «Als ich angekommen war, hatte der Film begonnen.» STEP 4: use «als» also for ages and periods of life: «Als ich zehn war …», «Als ich in Berlin lebte …» STEP 5: «als» is NEVER used for the present or the future (that's «wenn»).
o português usa «quando» para tudo. O al: English uses "when" for everything. German splits it: «als» for once in the past, «wenn» for everything else — and «wann» only for questions. Tip: if you could say "whenever", it's «wenn».
Wenn ich Kind war, wohnte ich im Dorf.
Als ich Kind war, wohnte ich im Dorf.
Depois da subordinada, o verbo na 2ª pos: After the subordinate clause, the verb in 2nd position.

Wenn ich Zeit habe, rufe ich an.

Wenn: o que se repete, o presente e o fu: Wenn: things that repeat, the present and the future
PASSO 1: «WENN» (quando, se) liga a prin: STEP 1: «WENN» (when, whenever, if) links the main clause to events that REPEAT, to the PRESENT and to the FUTURE: «Wenn ich Zeit habe, rufe ich dich an» (when I have time, I'll call you). STEP 2: for repetition IN THE PAST, German also uses «wenn», usually with «immer» or «jedes Mal» — English "whenever" or "used to": «Immer wenn ich Zeit hatte, bin ich zum See gegangen» (whenever I had time, I went to the lake). STEP 3: the choice: ONCE in the past → «als»; several times, or present/future → «wenn». STEP 4: the order is the same as in all subordinate clauses: verb at the end, main clause with the verb in 2nd position. STEP 5: remember «wenn» also means "if" (a condition): «Wenn es regnet, bleibe ich zu Hause.»

PASSO 1: «WÄHREND» (enquanto, durante) l: STEP 1: «WÄHREND» (while) links two things happening at the same time: «Während ich arbeite, hört er Musik» (while I work, he listens to music). STEP 2: «SEITDEM» (since — time): «Seitdem ich in Berlin wohne, spreche ich mehr Deutsch» (since I've been living in Berlin, I speak more German) — present tense, as with «seit». STEP 3: «BIS» (until): «Ich warte, bis du kommst» (I'll wait until you come). STEP 4: «SOBALD» (as soon as): «Sobald ich Zeit habe, rufe ich an.» STEP 5: «SOLANGE» (as long as): «Solange es regnet, bleiben wir hier.» STEP 6: all of them open subordinate clauses with the verb at the END; after them, the main clause starts with the verb.
